vars.SUB: Fifteen extra days buys another reduction down the street, a softer appraisal, and a buyer with more to compare you against.

vars.TITLE: Keeping the house, alone
vars.LINES:
"I'll just refinance."
Easy plan. Hard math.
[[gap]]
One income now, not two.
A fresh appraisal.
The other spouse still on
the loan until it funds.
[[gap]]
Check first: can you [[circle]]qualify?[[/circle]]
vars.NOTE: -> your lender and attorney own the actual numbers.

vars.HEADLINE:
Call The Insurer
Before You Write
vars.DECK: Roof age, wood-shake, defensible space, distance to a hydrant — any of it can change what the loan looks like. Ask before the offer, not the week before closing.

vars.TITLE: Three heirs, one house
vars.LINES:
One wants to keep it.
Who says what it's worth?
[[gap]]
Not a guess.
Not the assessor's number.
An independent [[circle]]appraisal[[/circle]]
is where it starts.
vars.NOTE: -> confirm valuation and payout with the estate's attorney.

vars.HEADLINE:
Closings
[[i]]around camp[[/i]]
vars.SUB: Archery opened September 5. Backcountry rifle is already in. Half the valley is out of cell range till Sunday night.
Listings that take one clean reduction early are closing closer to their number than the ones waiting two weeks to cut small.

vars.TAG: West and Company · How We Work
vars.HEADLINE:
Silence On The Radio
Is Never Good News
vars.DECK: Every client gets a standing update the same day each week, news or no news. Three weeks of silence is what makes people assume the worst.
